references: Jung et al. 2021 Algorithmic Recourse under Imperfect Causal Knowledge
Nabi & Shpitser 2018 Fair Inference on Outcomes
Karimi et al. 2021 Algorithmic Recourse: from Counterfactual Explanations to Interventions

provenance.base: instruction.md 6.1, reproduced verbatim: the 7 nodes and all 14 edges of the specified graph are present unchanged
provenance.reason: The 6-feature graph of 6.1 caps the black box at test AUC 0.887, below the 0.90 acceptance criterion of 5.2. The three added nodes are genuine Adult columns; adding them (never removing a specified node or edge) reaches AUC 0.918 while keeping the causal story intact.

notes: income is a sink: no intervention may target a descendant of the prediction, so the SCM has no outgoing edge from income.
capital_gain and capital_loss are placed downstream of age/education/occupation (investable surplus follows earning capacity) and upstream of income (realised gains are part of taxable income).
No edge is drawn between workclass and occupation: both are children of education and the direction between them is not identifiable from domain knowledge alone.
No age -> income edge is asserted, following 6.1: the effect of age on income is mediated by education, occupation, hours and capital.
gender -> {occupation, hours_per_week, income} encodes the labour-market discrimination paths; they are kept so the fairness analysis can quantify them, not because they are desirable.
